quests.instruction: A friend hands you tea while you're stressed about an exam.
quests.word: You'll be fine, you always are.
quests.textToSpeak: You'll be fine, you always are.
options: Slow, warm fall on 'are' — genuine reassurance
Fall-rise on 'are' — a hint of doubt
quests.correctAnswer: Slow, warm fall on 'are' — genuine reassurance
quests.hint: The friend wants to calm you. Which ending shows that she believes it?
quests.explanation: A slow, warm fall shows that the speaker has no reservations. A fall-rise would suggest a quiet 'but'.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 Real reassurance settles slowly and warmly.

quests.instruction: In a noisy workshop, your supervisor looks at the unfinished job and says this to no one in particular.
quests.word: Are we going to finish this today, or not?
quests.textToSpeak: Are we going to finish this today, or not?
options: Rising — genuine question about the schedule
Falling, sharp — impatient, not really a question
quests.correctAnswer: Falling, sharp — impatient, not really a question
quests.hint: Look at who is speaking and why. Does the supervisor actually expect anyone to answer?
quests.explanation: A sharp fall shows that the speaker is making a point, not asking. A rise would ask sincerely.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A yes/no question can fall when it is really a complaint.

quests.instruction: A new neighbor introduces herself, and you want to sound welcoming, not nosy.
quests.word: What brings you to this part of town?
quests.textToSpeak: What brings you to this part of town?
options: Firm fall — probing interview tone
Light rise — friendly interest
quests.correctAnswer: Light rise — friendly interest
quests.hint: WH-questions usually fall. Which delivery makes this one friendly?
quests.explanation: A light rise softens the WH-question and shows casual interest. A fall would sound more like an interview.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 A light rise can make a WH-question friendlier.

quests.instruction: A stranger at the bus stop asks whether it is always this late.
quests.word: Only on days that matter.
quests.textToSpeak: Only on days that matter.
options: Flat, slightly weary fall — dry humor
Warm, lifted rise — encouraging small talk
quests.correctAnswer: Flat, slightly weary fall — dry humor
quests.hint: This is a joke, delivered without smiling. Which delivery sells it?
quests.explanation: A flat, weary fall makes the humor dry. A warm rise would sound encouraging.
quests.pitchRule: 😏 Dry humor is flat and quick.

quests.instruction: Your manager thanks you for staying late, and you're tired but professional.
quests.word: No problem, happy to help.
quests.textToSpeak: No problem, happy to help.
options: Bright, wide fall — genuinely happy
Level, even, quick — polite but flat
quests.correctAnswer: Level, even, quick — polite but flat
quests.hint: The words are enthusiastic; the situation isn't. Which delivery reflects both?
quests.explanation: A level, even delivery keeps the phrase polite but shows a lack of real enthusiasm. A wide fall would sound genuine.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Formulaic phrases go flat when the feeling isn't there.

quests.instruction: You've just heard that a deal fell through after months of work.
quests.word: So all those months, for nothing?
quests.textToSpeak: So all those months, for nothing?
options: Rise on 'months', falling 'nothing' — bitter
Rising throughout — genuine question
quests.correctAnswer: Rise on 'months', falling 'nothing' — bitter
quests.hint: There are two clauses. Which one carries the bitterness?
quests.explanation: A rise on 'months' opens the complaint and a fall on 'nothing' delivers the bitter conclusion. A rise throughout would ask for information.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 A bitter rhetorical question ends on a fall.

quests.instruction: Your sister asks whether you are coming to her recital. You are, and you tease her.
quests.word: Oh, I guess I can pencil you in.
quests.textToSpeak: Oh, I guess I can pencil you in.
options: Lift on 'guess', playful fall — teasing
Flat fall — genuinely reluctant
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'guess', playful fall — teasing
quests.hint: The words sound reluctant, but the situation suggests otherwise. Which delivery agrees with the situation?
quests.explanation: A lift on 'guess' and a playful fall show that you are joking. A flat fall would sound sincerely reluctant.
quests.pitchRule: 😏 Playful teasing uses lifts and a light fall.

quests.instruction: An interviewer asks about your weaknesses.
quests.word: I tend to take on too much, which I'm working on.
quests.textToSpeak: I tend to take on too much, which I'm working on.
options: Lift on 'much', lowered fall on 'on' — honest, humble
Bright rise on 'much', wide ending — proud boasting
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'much', lowered fall on 'on' — honest, humble
quests.hint: A weakness should sound sincere, not proud. Which delivery matches?
quests.explanation: A lift on 'much' opens the admission, and a lowered fall shows that you're serious about improving. A bright rise would sound like a boast.
quests.pitchRule: 🤝 A humble admission lands low.

quests.instruction: You overhear colleagues gossiping and want to change the subject gently.
quests.word: Anyway, how did the presentation go?
quests.textToSpeak: Anyway, how did the presentation go?
options: Fall on 'anyway', rise on 'go' — a yes/no question
Lift on 'anyway', fall on 'go' — smooth topic change
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'anyway', fall on 'go' — smooth topic change
quests.hint: The phrase 'anyway' marks a shift. Which ending completes it?
quests.explanation: A lift on 'anyway' signals the switch, and a fall on 'go' asks an open question about the presentation. A rise would turn it into yes or no.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A topic change lifts on its marker and falls on its question.

quests.instruction: You have to interrupt a colleague who is running over time.
quests.word: Sorry, I'm going to have to stop you there.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, I'm going to have to stop you there.
options: Rise on 'there' — tentative
Fall on 'there' — polite but firm
quests.correctAnswer: Fall on 'there' — polite but firm
quests.hint: The apology is polite, but the action is not optional. Which ending shows that?
quests.explanation: A fall on 'there' keeps the politeness but makes the interruption firm. A rise would make it sound like a request.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A polite interruption still lands on a fall.

quests.instruction: Your friend is leaving her job to travel, and you're worried but supportive.
quests.word: That's a big step. Are you sure you're ready?
quests.textToSpeak: That's a big step. Are you sure you're ready?
options: Level fall on 'step', soft rise on 'ready' — concerned support
Sharp fall on 'step', flat on 'ready' — disapproval
quests.correctAnswer: Level fall on 'step', soft rise on 'ready' — concerned support
quests.hint: There are two sentences, and the second is a question. Which delivery shows care?
quests.explanation: A soft rise on 'ready' shows that you want a real answer and care about it. A flat second sentence would sound like judgment.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 Concern softens the closing question.

quests.instruction: A friend has done something generous for you.
quests.word: I can't believe you did that for me.
quests.textToSpeak: I can't believe you did that for me.
options: Wide, warm fall — moved gratitude
Sharp rise — accusation
quests.correctAnswer: Wide, warm fall — moved gratitude
quests.hint: The words can express awe or anger. Which delivery fits the situation?
quests.explanation: A wide, warm fall shows that the speaker is touched. A sharp rise would sound accusing.
quests.pitchRule: 😊 Gratitude is wide and warm.

quests.instruction: You're presenting quarterly numbers, and pause for effect between sentences.
quests.word: Revenue was up. Costs were down. And we still missed the target.
quests.textToSpeak: Revenue was up. Costs were down. And we still missed the target.
options: Three even, identical falls in a row — flat list
Two short falls, then a slower, lower fall — twist
quests.correctAnswer: Two short falls, then a slower, lower fall — twist
quests.hint: The last sentence changes the meaning of the first two. Which delivery prepares for the twist?
quests.explanation: Two short, bright falls set up the good news. A slower, lower last fall signals the twist.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A twist sits on a slower, lower fall.

quests.instruction: You're frustrated that a plan was delayed for weeks.
quests.word: If it were up to me, we'd have started weeks ago.
quests.textToSpeak: If it were up to me, we'd have started weeks ago.
options: Bright fall on 'ago', no stress on 'weeks' — cheerful
Lift on 'me', stress on 'weeks', fall on 'ago' — frustrated
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'me', stress on 'weeks', fall on 'ago' — frustrated
quests.hint: The sentence has an unspoken complaint. Which word carries it?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'weeks' shows how long the delay felt. A bright fall would ignore the frustration.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Frustration stresses the duration.

quests.instruction: You're describing a risky idea to a colleague.
quests.word: I'm not saying it's impossible, just unlikely.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not saying it's impossible, just unlikely.
options: Peaks on 'impossible' and 'unlikely' — contrast in degree
Peaks on 'saying' and 'just' — the framing wording
quests.correctAnswer: Peaks on 'impossible' and 'unlikely' — contrast in degree
quests.hint: The speaker compares two degrees of difficulty. Which words carry the contrast?
quests.explanation: 'Impossible' and 'unlikely' are the two degrees, so they take the peaks. 'Saying' and 'just' are framing words.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 Contrasted degrees carry the peaks.

quests.instruction: A friend asks you to promise not to tell a secret, and you tease them.
quests.word: Have I ever told a secret?
quests.textToSpeak: Have I ever told a secret?
options: Rising, even — a genuine, serious question
Falling, light — playful rhetorical question
quests.correctAnswer: Falling, light — playful rhetorical question
quests.hint: The friend knows the answer. How seriously is the question meant?
quests.explanation: A light fall on 'secret' shows that the question is playful and that you expect 'no'. A rise would ask sincerely.
quests.pitchRule: 😏 A light fall turns a yes/no question into a tease.

quests.instruction: A waiter offers you a drink.
quests.word: And for you, still or sparkling?
quests.textToSpeak: And for you, still or sparkling?
options: Rise on 'still', fall on 'sparkling' — choice
Rise on both words — open question, other drinks
quests.correctAnswer: Rise on 'still', fall on 'sparkling' — choice
quests.hint: Recall the pattern from choice questions. How do these two options end?
quests.explanation: Two named options use a rise on the first and a fall on the last. Both rising would not mark a choice.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A waiter's two options follow the rise-fall pattern.

quests.instruction: You comfort a friend after a breakup.
quests.word: You don't have to talk about it if you don't want to.
quests.textToSpeak: You don't have to talk about it if you don't want to.
options: Slow, low, gentle fall — permission and care
Bright, quick fall — cheerful, brisk reassurance
quests.correctAnswer: Slow, low, gentle fall — permission and care
quests.hint: This is a gentle offer. Which delivery makes it feel safe?
quests.explanation: A slow, low fall shows care and gives space. A bright fall would sound cheerful and misplaced.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 Care is slow, low and gentle.

quests.instruction: Your friend says he sold his car to fund a trip to Iceland.
quests.word: You did what?
quests.textToSpeak: You did what?
options: Low fall on 'what' — angry disapproval
High rise on 'what' — stunned echo
quests.correctAnswer: High rise on 'what' — stunned echo
quests.hint: The speaker heard exactly what was said. What is the question really expressing?
quests.explanation: A high rise on 'what' repeats the shocking news in disbelief. A low fall would sound angry.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 A high rise on the WH-word signals disbelief.

quests.instruction: A manager has heard several complaints about an employee.
quests.word: I'll have a word with him.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll have a word with him.
options: Light, quick fall — casual
Level, firm fall — serious intent
quests.correctAnswer: Level, firm fall — serious intent
quests.hint: The phrase can be casual or serious. Which delivery matches the situation?
quests.explanation: A level, firm fall shows that the manager takes it seriously. A light, quick fall would sound like a passing remark.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 Serious intent uses a level, firm fall.

quests.instruction: Someone shows you the room they arranged, and it's not what you hoped for.
quests.word: It's not exactly what I had in mind, but it'll do.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not exactly what I had in mind, but it'll do.
options: Bright fall on 'mind' and on 'do' — pleased approval
Lift on 'mind', low fall on 'do' — resigned acceptance
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'mind', low fall on 'do' — resigned acceptance
quests.hint: There's a limit followed by an acceptance. Which delivery matches?
quests.explanation: A lift on 'mind' opens the reservation, and a low fall on 'do' shows resigned acceptance. A bright fall would sound pleased.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 Resigned acceptance lands low.

quests.instruction: You're leaving a voicemail for a client after a mistake on your side.
quests.word: Hi Ms Lindqvist, it's Omar. I wanted to apologize personally for the delay.
quests.textToSpeak: Hi Ms Lindqvist, it's Omar. I wanted to apologize personally for the delay.
options: Slow, lowered fall on 'delay' — sincere apology
Bright, quick fall on 'delay' — routine apology
quests.correctAnswer: Slow, lowered fall on 'delay' — sincere apology
quests.hint: The apology is the point. Which delivery makes it sincere?
quests.explanation: A slow, lowered fall shows that the apology is real. A bright, quick delivery would sound like a form letter.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A sincere apology is slower and lower.

quests.instruction: A teenager says 'I'm fine' when they are clearly not.
quests.word: You don't sound fine to me.
quests.textToSpeak: You don't sound fine to me.
options: Soft, low fall — caring observation
Sharp fall — accusation
quests.correctAnswer: Soft, low fall — caring observation
quests.hint: You want to open a door, not confront. Which delivery is gentle?
quests.explanation: A soft, low fall makes the observation caring and invites conversation. A sharp fall would sound like an accusation.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 Caring observations are soft and low.

quests.instruction: You finish explaining a complicated process and want to check.
quests.word: Does that make more sense, or should I go through it again?
quests.textToSpeak: Does that make more sense, or should I go through it again?
options: Rise on 'sense', fall on 'again' — offering a choice
Rise on 'sense' and on 'again' — open question, one answer
quests.correctAnswer: Rise on 'sense', fall on 'again' — offering a choice
quests.hint: There are two options in the sentence. Which ending offers them?
quests.explanation: A rise on 'sense' and a fall on 'again' mark the two options. Both rising would leave the question open.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 An offer of two choices follows the rise-fall pattern.

quests.instruction: A friend describes a travel mishap and asks what you would have done.
quests.word: Honestly? I'd have taken the next flight home.
quests.textToSpeak: Honestly? I'd have taken the next flight home.
options: Fall on 'honestly', rise on 'home' — tentative
Rise on 'honestly', firm fall on 'home' — candid opinion
quests.correctAnswer: Rise on 'honestly', firm fall on 'home' — candid opinion
quests.hint: The speaker is being direct. Which delivery shows confidence?
quests.explanation: A rise on 'honestly' draws attention, and a firm fall on 'home' delivers the opinion. A rise at the end would make it tentative.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A candid opinion ends with a firm fall.

quests.instruction: Someone compliments your talk and you deflect it modestly.
quests.word: Oh, that's kind, but the team did most of the work.
quests.textToSpeak: Oh, that's kind, but the team did most of the work.
options: Flat on 'kind' and on 'work' — dismissive reply
Warm lift on 'kind', fall on 'work' — modest deflection
quests.correctAnswer: Warm lift on 'kind', fall on 'work' — modest deflection
quests.hint: The praise is kindly declined. Which delivery keeps things warm?
quests.explanation: A warm lift on 'kind' keeps the modesty polite, and a fall on 'work' shares the credit. A flat delivery would sound dismissive.
quests.pitchRule: 🤝 Modesty is warm at the start and firm at the end.

quests.instruction: At a family dinner, your uncle repeats a rumor about your cousin.
quests.word: And where did you hear that?
quests.textToSpeak: And where did you hear that?
options: Low, flat fall — challenging
Bright fall — curious
quests.correctAnswer: Low, flat fall — challenging
quests.hint: The question isn't neutral. Which delivery shows that?
quests.explanation: A low, flat fall makes the question a challenge to the source. A bright fall would sound curious.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 A flat, low fall can turn a WH-question into a challenge.

quests.instruction: A colleague hands you a resignation letter and says nothing else. You look up.
quests.word: You're leaving?
quests.textToSpeak: You're leaving?
options: Low, slow rise — quiet shock
High, quick rise — excited surprise
quests.correctAnswer: Low, slow rise — quiet shock
quests.hint: The situation is emotional, but the sentence is short. Which delivery shows what you feel?
quests.explanation: A low, slow rise shows quiet shock, and the pace shows that you are absorbing it. A high, quick rise would sound excited.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 Quiet shock is slow and low.

quests.instruction: After a very long project, the team finally ships. You speak quietly to your manager.
quests.word: We actually did it.
quests.textToSpeak: We actually did it.
options: Quick, narrow fall — routine report
Slow, wide fall on 'did it' — awed relief
quests.correctAnswer: Slow, wide fall on 'did it' — awed relief
quests.hint: The moment is emotional but quiet. Which delivery carries it?
quests.explanation: A slow, wide fall shows awe and relief. A quick, narrow fall would sound like a status update.
quests.pitchRule: 😮‍💨 Awed relief is slow and wide.

quests.instruction: You must tell your team that a client is pulling out.
quests.word: I've got some news, and it's not what we hoped for.
quests.textToSpeak: I've got some news, and it's not what we hoped for.
options: Bright, quick fall on 'news' and 'for' — casual update
Lift on 'news', slow, lowered fall on 'for' — careful bad news
quests.correctAnswer: Lift on 'news', slow, lowered fall on 'for' — careful bad news
quests.hint: The team needs to be prepared. Which delivery does that?
quests.explanation: A lift on 'news' prepares the listeners, and a slow, lowered fall on 'for' delivers the message gently. A bright delivery would clash with it.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 Bad news is delivered slowly and low.
